knowledge_point.title: Finding a General Solution in Explicit Form

question.:question/problem:
Find the general solution to $\frac{\mathrm{d}p}{\mathrm{d}t}=3e^{-p}.$

$p=\ln($ {{field-1}} $+C)$, where $C$ is an arbitrary real constant.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we separate variables and integrate both sides with respect to $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}e^p\,\frac{\mathrm{d}p}{\mathrm{d}t} & =3 \\ \int e^p\,\mathrm{d}p & =\int 3\,\mathrm{d}t \\ e^p & =3 t+C\end{aligned}
$$

This is a general solution in implicit form. Solving for $p$ gives

$$
p=\ln(3 t+C)
$$

Work on intervals where the logarithm argument is positive.

knowledge_point.title: Finding a General Solution in Explicit Form

question.:question/problem:
Find the general solution to $\frac{\mathrm{d}T}{\mathrm{d}t}=-0.03(T-35)$ for $T\ne 35.$

$T=35+K\cdot$ {{field-1}}, where $K$ is an arbitrary nonzero constant.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we separate variables and integrate both sides with respect to $t,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}T}{\text{d}t} & =-0.03(T-35) \\ \frac{1}{T-35}\cdot \frac{\text{d}T}{\text{d}t} & =-0.03 \\ \int \frac{1}{T-35}\cdot \frac{\text{d}T}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t & =\int -0.03\,\text{d}t \\ \int \frac{\text{d}T}{T-35} & =-0.03\int \,\text{d}t \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡|T-35| & =-0.03t+C\end{aligned}
$$

This is a perfectly valid general solution. However, if we want to write $T=T(t)$ explicitly, then we can solve for $T.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡|T-35| & =-0.03t+C \\ |T-35| & ={e}^{-0.03t+C} \\ |T-35| & =K\,{e}^{-0.03t}\end{aligned}
$$

where $K={e}^{C}$ is an arbitrary positive constant.

We can drop the absolute value bars by allowing $K$ to be both positive and negative. Therefore, the most general solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =35+K\,{e}^{-0.03t}.\end{aligned}
$$
